summary: The candidate is not mathematically well-formed as submitted. Essential LaTeX in the selected-rank definition and in the good-class mass calculation is corrupted, so the rank in (19), the identity in (44), and the deductions depending on them cannot be verified without repairing the candidate.
critical_errors: Equation (19) does not impose a well-formed affine-map condition on the minimization variable: its subscript is split into an incomplete expression ending in 'm affine'. Thus r_i^{sel} is not rigorously defined as written, and conclusion (20) has an undefined parameter.

Equation (44) starts with 'rac{gamma_d}{4}' instead of a valid coefficient and uses a corrupted summation qualifier. Consequently (44) is not a valid mathematical identity, so the Cauchy-Schwarz calculation (45)-(47), the lower mass bound in (23), and the later conclusions that depend on that bound do not follow from the submitted proof.
gaps: The same malformed good-class qualifier occurs in (41), (45), and (46), leaving B_i^g and the domains of the sums in that part of the proof unspecified as written.
repair_hints: Regenerate equations (19), (41), and (44)-(46) with correctly escaped, well-formed LaTeX, then rerun the full stateless verification; the verifier may not silently supply the apparent intended formulas.
